summary: Visually inspected every row of contact sheets 000-008 (108 station pairs, 216 directional images). Readable roadside wall/bank forms recur throughout. Lower banks and open coastal composition are more common in sheets 003-006; sheets 000-001 and 007-008 repeatedly show large near or upper faces. Dominant-wall presence requires a substantial readable face, not merely any distant rock. Side labels refer to substantial readable roadside terrain, not thin verges; near_profile is the strongest observation of the pair, not correspondence of a single physical surface. A panorama may coexist with a dominant face. Presence/absence applies only to inspected images. Diagnostic colours were not treated as natural material classes. The contact-sheet observations remain AI proposals; four selected original PNG checks are recorded separately. This is not full original-PNG coverage, canonical human review, world footprints, GEO_FIX findings, D assignments or background-simplification approval. C was refined independently: the skyline of a B face alone and a bare sea horizon do not establish a separate C terrain region. Distinct coastal outcrops/landscape regions remain C candidates; borderline separation is uncertain. Near-side fields exclude flat shoulders and thin verges. Four requested original PNGs were visually inspected; station74 dominant-face classification and station100 forward near-side extent were refined, with C removed where only the dominant face or roadside forms supply the outline. Final side-code alignment: near_sides records only raised roadside wall/bank forms, excluding descending ground faces, flat shoulders and parapets. Descending contact may still need A detail and remains in the written reason. Unresolved raised-side extent at a bend is marked uncertain. No near_profile or B/C classification changed during this alignment.
